questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Write a precise definition of a circle. Use only the words point, plane, and distance, and words built from them.
questions.prompt_markup: Write a precise definition of a circle. Use only the words point, plane, and distance, and words built from them.
questions.correct_answer: A circle is the set of all points in a plane that are a given distance (the radius) from a given point in that plane (the center).
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent wording. Essential: (1) ALL points, (2) in one plane, (3) at one fixed distance, (4) from one fixed point, the center. Not accepted: "a round shape" (not precise); leaving out the plane (that describes a sphere); "points within a distance" (that is a disk).

questions.prompt: Points A and B lie on line ℓ. Which is a precise definition of segment AB?
questions.prompt_markup: Points A and B lie on line ℓ. Which is a precise definition of segment AB?

choices.text: Points A and B together with every point C of line ℓ for which AC + CB = AB
Point A and every point of line ℓ on the same side of A as B
Every point of the plane that is closer to A than to B

questions.correct_answer: Points A and B together with every point C of line ℓ for which AC + CB = AB
questions.grading_note: A segment is its two endpoints and every point between them; "C is between A and B" means C is on the line and AC + CB = AB (distance along a line). The other choices describe line ℓ, ray AB, and a half-plane.

questions.prompt: Write a precise definition of an angle. Name its vertex and its sides in your definition.
questions.prompt_markup: Write a precise definition of an angle. Name its vertex and its sides in your definition.
questions.correct_answer: An angle is the figure formed by two rays that have the same endpoint. The common endpoint is the vertex, and the two rays are the sides.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent wording. Essential: two rays (not lines), one common endpoint, that endpoint named as the vertex. Not accepted: "the space between two lines", "a turn", or "two lines that cross" (two crossing lines form four angles).

questions.prompt: Proposed definition: "A circle is a set of points that are all the same distance from a point O." Give a set that fits this wording but is NOT a circle.
questions.prompt_markup:
Proposed definition: "A circle is a set of points that are all the same distance from a point O."
Give a set that fits this wording but is NOT a circle.
questions.correct_answer: For example, two points that are each 3 cm from O (or an arc of a circle, or a sphere). The definition must say ALL points at that distance, in one plane.
questions.grading_note: Any set that fits the wording but is not a whole circle: finitely many points, an arc, or a sphere.

questions.prompt: Proposed definition: "Point M is the midpoint of segment AB if AM = MB." Give a counterexample, and repair the definition.

Proposed definition: "Point M is the midpoint of segment AB if AM = MB."
